translationRepairs.before: Murong Huang of Former Yan.
translationRepairs.after: Murong Huang.
translationRepairs.reason: s0002 is only the name 慕容皝; “of Former Yan” is not in the Chinese and is an editorial gloss, so the shorter “Murong Huang.” matches the source.

translationRepairs.before: In the beginning, Huang’s elder half-brother by a concubine, Jianwei Han, was fierce in arms and had heroic talent; plain was envied by Huang; younger brothers by the same mother, Ren the Campaign General and Zhao the Guangwu general, both had favor with Hui; Huang also was not even toward them.
translationRepairs.after: In the beginning, Huang’s elder half-brother by a concubine, Jianwei Han, was fierce in arms and had heroic talent; he had long been envied by Huang; younger brothers by the same mother, Ren the Campaign General and Zhao the Guangwu general, both had favor with Hui; Huang also was not even toward them.
translationRepairs.reason: 素為皝所忌 means Han had long/always been resented by Huang; rendering 素 as “plain” is a mistranslation, and “he had long been envied by Huang” restores the adverb.

translationRepairs.before: Huang executed Zhao and sent agents to probe Ren, meeting him at the Xiandu defile.
translationRepairs.after: Huang executed Zhao and sent envoys to probe whether Ren’s situation was genuine; they encountered Ren at Xiandu.
translationRepairs.reason: 遣使按檢仁之虛實，遇仁於險瀆 has the envoys, not Huang, meet Ren at 險瀆; 仁知事發，殺皝使 confirms they, not Huang, encountered him. The original dangling “meeting him” misattributes the subject.

translationRepairs.before: Huang sent his younger brother Jianwei You, marshal Tong Shou, and others to campaign against him.
translationRepairs.after: Huang sent his younger brother Jianwu You, marshal Tong Shou, and others to campaign against him.
translationRepairs.reason: The title on You is 建武, not 建威 (Han’s title in s0011); “Jianwu You” corrects the literal mix-up.

translationRepairs.before: Ten days later Duan Lan and Murong Han (the kinsman who had joined Duan Liao) again besieged Liucheng; Huang sent Murong Han, who held the title of general who pacifies the distance, together with Feng Yi, to relieve the city.
translationRepairs.after: Ten-odd days later Duan Lan and Murong Han, the kinsman who had joined Duan Liao, again besieged Liucheng; Huang sent the Ningyuan general, a different Murong Han, together with Feng Yi and others to relieve the city.
translationRepairs.reason: 蘭、翰復圍柳城 names the besieger 翰, while 皝遣甯遠慕容汗及封弈等救之 names a different man 汗. The proposal is right to split them and restore 甯遠 and 等, but its English still collides two homophones and inserts Chinese characters; 旬余 is “ten-odd days,” not “ten days.”

translationRepairs.before: Early in Xiankang he sent Feng Yi against the Yuwen chieftain Sheyiyu and returned with rich spoils.
translationRepairs.after: Early in Xiankang he sent Feng Yi against Sheyiyu of a separate Yuwen division and returned with rich spoils.
translationRepairs.reason: 宇文別部涉奕於 identifies Sheyiyu with a Yuwen detached division, not as chieftain of the Yuwen as a whole; the proposed phrasing matches 別部.

translationRepairs.before: Huang met them with fifty thousand foot and horse; both enemy columns fled from Liucheng.
translationRepairs.after: Huang met them with fifty thousand foot and horse; Lan and Gui both fled when the army halted at Liucheng.
translationRepairs.reason: 師次柳城，蘭、歸皆遁 names Lan and Gui and has Huang’s army halt at Liucheng before they flee; “both enemy columns fled from Liucheng” drops the names and misplaces the flight.

translationRepairs.before: Feng Yi urged that Huang’s duties outweighed his title, so in Xiankang 3 he assumed the kingship of Yan and proclaimed an amnesty.
translationRepairs.after: Feng Yi and others, holding that Huang’s burden was heavy while his rank was light, urged him to style himself King of Yan; Huang thereupon in the third year of Xiankang illegitimately assumed the kingship and pardoned those within his borders.
translationRepairs.reason: 封弈等 records a group of advisers, 僭即王位 is the historian’s mark of illegitimate accession, and 赦其境內 is a pardon inside his borders; the original omits 等 and 僭 and flattens the amnesty.

translationRepairs.before: He sent Murong Ke with two thousand horse in a dawn sally.
translationRepairs.after: He sent his son Ke and others with two thousand horse in a dawn sally.
translationRepairs.reason: 遣子恪等 explicitly calls Ke Huang’s son and includes companions; “Murong Ke” alone drops both 子 and 等.

translationRepairs.before: The court promoted him to general who campaigns north, governor of Youzhou, concurrent Pingzhou, cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, with ten thousand extra households and unchanged barbarian titles.
translationRepairs.after: The emperor again sent envoys to advance Huang as General Who Campaigns North, shepherd of You Province, concurrently governor of Ping Province, adding Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and an increase of ten thousand households, with credentials, overall command, shanyu, and duke as before.
translationRepairs.reason: 帝又遣使 is the emperor sending envoys again, not a vague “court” promotion; 持節、都督、單于、公如故 are specific remaining titles, not “unchanged barbarian titles.”

translationRepairs.before: Murong Ping crushed Shi Cheng in western Liaodong, slew Huyan Huang and Zhang Zhi, and brought home a thousand captives.
translationRepairs.after: Huang’s forward commander Murong Ping defeated Shi Hu’s generals Shi Cheng and others in Liaoxi, slew Huyan Huang and Zhang Zhi, and brought home more than a thousand households.
translationRepairs.reason: 遼西 is Liaoxi, not western Liaodong; 皝前軍帥, 季龍將石成等, and 掠千餘戶 are also in the Chinese and are omitted or altered (“captives”) in the original idiomatic sentence.

translationRepairs.before: Huang’s forward commander Murong Ping defeated Jilong’s generals Shi Cheng and others in western Liaodong, beheaded their generals Huyan Huang, Zhang Zhi, plundered over a thousand households and returned.
translationRepairs.after: Huang’s forward commander Murong Ping defeated Jilong’s generals Shi Cheng and others in Liaoxi, beheaded their generals Huyan Huang and Zhang Zhi, plundered over a thousand households and returned.
translationRepairs.reason: The same 遼西 is the commandery Liaoxi, not “western Liaodong”; the proposed literal correction is accurate.

translationRepairs.before: Huang opened Gao Zhen’s father’s tomb, carried off the coffin, the queen, treasures, and fifty thousand captives, fired the palaces, and razed Wandu.
translationRepairs.after: Huang opened Gao Zhen’s father Li’s tomb, carried off the corpse together with Zhen’s mother, wife, and treasures, plundered more than fifty thousand men and women, fired the palaces, and razed Wandu.
translationRepairs.reason: 釗父利墓 names the father 利; 載其屍並其母妻珍寶 is the corpse plus Zhen’s mother and wife, not a coffin and “the queen”; 掠男女五萬餘口 is more than fifty thousand men and women.

translationRepairs.before: Next year Gao Zhen sent tribute and his father’s body was returned.
translationRepairs.after: The next year Gao Zhen sent envoys declaring himself a subject of Huang, offered local products, and Huang then returned his father’s corpse.
translationRepairs.reason: 釗遣使稱臣于皝，貢其方物，乃歸其父屍 records submission to Huang, tribute of local products, and Huang’s subsequent return of the corpse; the original drops 稱臣 and the agent of 歸.

translationRepairs.before: Your Highness, with heroic and sage endowment, has been able to extend the former enterprise: south you crushed strong Zhao, east you destroyed Goguryeo, opened three thousand li of border and increased households by a hundred thousand, continuing the martial achievement of Murong Wu and Murong Guang, rivaling the great Earl of the West.
translationRepairs.after: Your Highness, with heroic and sage endowment, has been able to extend the former enterprise: south you crushed strong Zhao, east you destroyed Goguryeo, opened three thousand li of border and increased households by a hundred thousand, continuing the merit of martial expansion, rivaling the great Earl of the West.
translationRepairs.reason: 繼武闡廣之功 is a verbal phrase of continuing martial expansion, not personal names Murong Wu and Murong Guang. The proposal correctly rejects those inventions, but “martial work of expanding and broadening” is an awkward calque; “merit of martial expansion” is natural and faithful.

translationRepairs.before: You have fulfilled the hope of a happy land; the people of China will welcome you with food. Who can compare with Shi Hu!
translationRepairs.after: Recently you have deeply fulfilled the hope of a happy land; the people of China will all bring food to welcome you. Who then will remain with Shi Hu?
translationRepairs.reason: 石季龍誰與居乎 asks who would still dwell with Shi Hu once people bring food to welcome Huang, not who can compare with him; 邇者深副 and 皆將壺餐 are also restored.

translationRepairs.before: Even Wang Xian and Liu Ming, though punished, show my own lack of forbearance.
translationRepairs.after: Wang Xian and Liu Ming, although their offenses would warrant ban and dismissal, also show my own lack of forbearance.
translationRepairs.reason: 雖其罪應禁黜 is hypothetical desert: their offenses would warrant ban and dismissal; s0127 then restores their offices. “Though punished” treats the penalty as already inflicted.

translationRepairs.before: After Liucheng Duan Lan wanted to push on, but Murong Han feigned advice that spared Yan a deeper strike.
translationRepairs.after: After the defeat at Liucheng, Duan Lan wanted to push on, but Murong Han feigned advice that spared Yan a deeper strike.
translationRepairs.reason: 柳城之敗 is the defeat at Liucheng, followed by 段蘭 as a separate subject. Unpunctuated “After Liucheng Duan Lan” both drops 敗 and can be read as one name.

translationRepairs.before: When Duan Liao fell he fled north to Yuwen Gui.
translationRepairs.after: When Duan Liao fled in defeat, Han again went north to Yuwen Gui.
translationRepairs.reason: 及遼奔走，翰又北投宇文歸 has Liao’s flight as the circumstance and 翰 as the one who again went north to Yuwen Gui; the original makes Duan Liao the refugee.

translationRepairs.before: In the second year of Jianyuan, Huang followed to campaign against Yuwen Gui; on the line of battle was struck by a stray arrow; lay ill accumulated time.
translationRepairs.after: In the second year of Jianyuan, he followed Huang to campaign against Yuwen Gui; on the line of battle he was struck by a stray arrow; he lay ill a long time.
translationRepairs.reason: 從皝討宇文歸 means Han followed Huang on the campaign; the original makes Huang the follower and leaves the stray arrow without Han as subject.

translationRepairs.before: At the time Xianbei Shanyu Duan Juan was Jin’s General of Agile Cavalry, Duke of western Liaodong; by nature loved men of talent, humbly extended invitation to Yu.
translationRepairs.after: At the time Xianbei Shanyu Duan Juan was Jin’s General of Agile Cavalry and Duke of Liaoxi; by nature he loved men of talent and humbly invited Yu.
translationRepairs.reason: 遼西公 is Duke of Liaoxi, the same 遼西 as elsewhere, not “western Liaodong.”

translationRepairs.before: That year he invaded Goguryeo; King Gao Zhen sued for peace and he withdrew.
translationRepairs.after: That year he invaded Goguryeo; King Gao Zhao sued for peace and he withdrew.
translationRepairs.reason: 釗 is read Zhao (Gogugwon, Go Jo), not Zhen. The subject of 還 is 皝, and 'he withdrew' correctly refers to Huang, so no actor error remains.

translationRepairs.before: That year Huang campaigned against Gaogouli; King Gao Zhen begged alliance and returned.
translationRepairs.after: That year Huang campaigned against Gaogouli; King Gao Zhao begged a covenant, and Huang returned.
translationRepairs.reason: Fixes the name (釗 = Zhao). Also fixes the actor: in 乞盟而還 it is the campaigning Huang who returns, not the king. The proposal kept 'King ... returned', which is a definite subject error.

translationRepairs.before: The next year Gao Zhen sent his heir to pay homage to Huang.
translationRepairs.after: The next year Gao Zhao sent his heir to pay homage to Huang.
translationRepairs.reason: 釗 = Zhao. Rest is accurate.

translationRepairs.before: The next year, Zhen sent his heir apparent to court at Huang.
translationRepairs.after: The next year, Zhao sent his heir apparent to court at Huang.
translationRepairs.reason: The Goguryeo king's name 釗 is read Zhao, not Zhen (King Gogugwon, Go Jo). 'Zhen' is a misreading of 釗. Host should also check other chapters' renderings of 高句麗王釗.

translationRepairs.before: King Gao Zhen assumed the main thrust would come from the north, sent fifty thousand under his brother Wu to Beizhi, and held the southern defile with weaker troops.
translationRepairs.after: King Gao Zhao assumed the main thrust would come from the north, sent fifty thousand under his brother Wu to Beizhi, and held the southern defile with weaker troops.
translationRepairs.reason: 釗 = Zhao. Rest is accurate.

translationRepairs.before: Goguryeo King Zhen thought Huang’s army came by the northern route; thereupon sent his younger brother Wu leading picked fifty thousand to block Beizhi; personally led weak soldiers to guard the southern defile.
translationRepairs.after: Goguryeo King Zhao thought Huang’s army came by the northern route; thereupon sent his younger brother Wu leading picked fifty thousand to block Beizhi; personally led weak soldiers to guard the southern defile.
translationRepairs.reason: The Goguryeo king's name 釗 is read Zhao, not Zhen (King Gogugwon, Go Jo). 'Zhen' is a misreading of 釗. Host should also check other chapters' renderings of 高句麗王釗.

translationRepairs.before: Murong Han routed him at Mudi, pressed into Wandu, and Zhen fled alone on horseback.
translationRepairs.after: Murong Han routed him at Mudi, pressed into Wandu, and Zhao fled alone on horseback.
translationRepairs.reason: The Goguryeo king's name 釗 is read Zhao, not Zhen (King Gogugwon, Go Jo). 'Zhen' is a misreading of 釗. Host should also check other chapters' renderings of 高句麗王釗.

translationRepairs.before: Han fought Zhen at Mudi, greatly defeated them, rode victory then entered Wandu; Zhen single horse fled.
translationRepairs.after: Han fought Zhao at Mudi, greatly defeated them, rode victory then entered Wandu; Zhao single horse fled.
translationRepairs.reason: 釗 = Zhao; both occurrences fixed.

translationRepairs.before: Huang opened Gao Zhen’s father Li’s tomb, carried off the corpse together with Zhen’s mother, wife, and treasures, plundered more than fifty thousand men and women, fired the palaces, and razed Wandu.
translationRepairs.after: Huang opened Gao Zhao’s father Li’s tomb, carried off the corpse together with Zhao’s mother, wife, and treasures, plundered more than fifty thousand men and women, fired the palaces, razed Wandu, and returned.
translationRepairs.reason: The Chinese explicitly records Huang returning (而歸). Retain the independently accepted Zhao spelling and restore the return event in the idiomatic field, matching the literal field and primary text.

translationRepairs.before: Huang dug Zhen’s father Li’s tomb, loaded his corpse together with his mother, wife, and treasures, plundered over fifty thousand male and female, burned his palace chambers, destroyed Wandu and returned.
translationRepairs.after: Huang dug Zhao’s father Li’s tomb, loaded his corpse together with his mother, wife, and treasures, plundered over fifty thousand male and female, burned his palace chambers, destroyed Wandu and returned.
translationRepairs.reason: The Goguryeo king's name 釗 is read Zhao, not Zhen (King Gogugwon, Go Jo). 'Zhen' is a misreading of 釗. Host should also check other chapters' renderings of 高句麗王釗.

translationRepairs.before: The next year Gao Zhen sent envoys declaring himself a subject of Huang, offered local products, and Huang then returned his father’s corpse.
translationRepairs.after: The next year Gao Zhao sent envoys declaring himself a subject of Huang, offered local products, and Huang then returned his father’s corpse.
translationRepairs.reason: 釗 = Zhao. Huang as the subject of 歸 is correct.

translationRepairs.before: The next year, Zhen sent envoys declaring subject to Huang, offered their local products, then returned his father’s corpse.
translationRepairs.after: The next year, Zhao sent envoys declaring subject to Huang, offered their local products, then returned his father’s corpse.
translationRepairs.reason: 釗 = Zhao. The subjectless 'then returned' mirrors 乃歸 and is acceptable for the literal field.

translationRepairs.before: Shi Le asked, "If what you say is so, why did Prince Wang not employ him?"
translationRepairs.after: Shi Le asked, "If what you say is so, why did Duke Wang not employ him?"
translationRepairs.reason: 王公 means 'Lord/Duke Wang', meaning Wang Jun, whose term 王浚領州 appears in s0185. Wang Jun held a ducal fief, so Duke Wang is supported. 'Prince' is wrong.

translationRepairs.before: Le said: “If like your words, why did the prince duke not employ them?”
translationRepairs.after: Le said: “If like your words, why did Duke Wang not employ them?”
translationRepairs.reason: 王公 = Duke Wang (Wang Jun), not 'prince duke'.

translationRepairs.before: Song said: “The prince duke because he could not employ them, therefore became the enlightened lord’s captive.”
translationRepairs.after: Song said: “Duke Wang because he could not employ them, therefore became the enlightened lord’s captive.”
translationRepairs.reason: 王公 = Duke Wang (Wang Jun). The idiomatic field leaves 王公 implicit as 'he' and is correct.

translationRepairs.before: Magistrate Wang Bing of Xiangping and general Sun Ji turned Liaodong against him, while Feng Chou, Yi Yi, Han Jiao, Gao Xu, and others abandoned their posts and fled.
translationRepairs.after: Xiangping magistrate Wang Bing and general Sun Ji rebelled in Liaodong against Huang; Eastern Yi Colonel Feng Chou, Protector Yi Yi, Liaodong chancellor Han Jiao, Xuantu prefect Gao Xu, and others abandoned their cities and fled back.
translationRepairs.reason: Restores 叛於皝 (against Huang), the four offices, and 棄城奔還. This matches the source and the paired literal.

translationRepairs.before: Soon afterward Yuwen Qidegui was driven out by a rival kinsman, Yidougui, and died in exile; Huang led cavalry against Yidougui, who sued for peace; Huang then built Yuyin and Anjin and withdrew.
translationRepairs.after: Soon afterward Yuwen Qidegui was driven out by Yidougui of his separate division and died in exile; Huang led cavalry against Yidougui, who took fright and sued for peace; Huang then built the two cities of Yuyin and Anjin and withdrew.
translationRepairs.reason: 其別部逸豆歸 places Yidougui in a separate division of Qidegui's people. The text claims no kinship ('kinsman') and no leadership title ('separate-division leader'), so both are removed. Also restores 懼 and 二城.

translationRepairs.before: Recently you have deeply fulfilled the hope of a happy land; the people of China will all bring food to welcome you; with Shi Hu, who can compare!
translationRepairs.after: Recently you have deeply fulfilled the hope of a happy land; the people of China will all bring food to welcome you; Shi Jilong—who will dwell with him!
translationRepairs.reason: 誰與居乎 means 'who will stay with him', not 'who can compare'. Shi Jilong matches 石季龍 and the literal-field usage in s0060, s0087, s0158 and s0210. Shi Hu stays as a legitimate personal-name form in the idiomatic field.

translationRepairs.before: His elder half-brother Murong Han, who held the title general who establishes might, was a brilliant warrior whom Huang resented, while his full brothers Murong Ren and Murong Zhao, both favored by Hui, also stirred his jealousy.
translationRepairs.after: Earlier, Huang's elder half-brother Murong Han, general who establishes might, was brave in arms and of heroic talent, and Huang had long resented him. Huang's younger full brothers Murong Ren, general who campaigns against the caitiffs, and Murong Zhao, general who extends martial power, were both favored by Hui, which also displeased Huang.
translationRepairs.reason: Restore the flashback, long-standing jealousy, heroic talent, abbreviated military titles and younger maternal brothers explicitly attested by 初/素/有雄才/建威/征虜/廣武/母弟; preserve the named actors.

translationRepairs.before: In the beginning, Huang’s elder half-brother by a concubine, Jianwei Han, was fierce in arms and had heroic talent; he had long been envied by Huang; younger brothers by the same mother, Ren the Campaign General and Zhao the Guangwu general, both had favor with Hui; Huang also was not even toward them.
translationRepairs.after: At first, Huang's elder brother by a concubine, Han, the general who establishes might, was brave in warfare and had heroic talent; Huang had long been jealous of him. His younger brothers by the same mother, Ren, the general who campaigns against the caitiffs, and Zhao, the general who extends martial power, both enjoyed Hui's favor; Huang was also displeased with them.
translationRepairs.reason: Restore the flashback, long-standing jealousy, heroic talent, abbreviated military titles and younger maternal brothers explicitly attested by 初/素/有雄才/建威/征虜/廣武/母弟; preserve the named actors.

translationRepairs.before: Huang dispatched his brother Murong You and Marshal Tong Shou against him.
translationRepairs.after: Huang dispatched his younger brother Murong You, general who establishes martial power, Marshal Tong Shou, and others to campaign against Ren.
translationRepairs.reason: Restore the younger-brother relation and abbreviated military title of You (弟建武幼), the collective 等 and campaign 討之; the preceding/following Chinese identifies Ren as the target.

translationRepairs.before: Huang sent his younger brother Jianwu You, marshal Tong Shou, and others to campaign against him.
translationRepairs.after: Huang sent his younger brother You, the general who establishes martial power, marshal Tong Shou, and others to campaign against him.
translationRepairs.reason: Restore the younger-brother relation and abbreviated military title of You (弟建武幼), the collective 等 and campaign 討之; the preceding/following Chinese identifies Ren as the target.

translationRepairs.before: That year, Emperor Cheng sent attendants Xu Meng, Lüqiu Xing, and others bearing credentials to appoint Huang General Who Guards the Army, governor of Ping Province, Great Shanyu, Duke of Liaodong; bearer of credentials, overall commander, investiture by mandate on the model of Hui’s precedent.
translationRepairs.after: That year, Emperor Cheng sent the yezhe Xu Meng, Lüqiu Xing, and others bearing credentials to appoint Huang General Who Guards the Army, governor of Ping Province, Great Shanyu, and Duke of Liaodong; with credentials, overall command, and authority to make appointments under imperial mandate, just as in Hui’s precedent.
translationRepairs.reason: 謁者 is rendered as the office yezhe, restoring 遣謁者徐孟、閭丘幸等持節 and the three grants 持節、都督、承制封拜 with 一如廆故事; all offices and names preserved.

translationRepairs.before: That year Emperor Cheng invested him as general who guards the army, governor of Pingzhou, great shanyu, and duke of Liaodong, with full authority to enfeoff subordinates as Hui had held.
translationRepairs.after: That year Emperor Cheng sent the envoys Xu Meng, Lüqiu Xing, and others with credentials to invest Huang as General Who Guards the Army, governor of Ping Province, great shanyu, and duke of Liaodong, with credentials, overall command, and authority to enfeoff by mandate, as Hui had held.
translationRepairs.reason: Restores 遣謁者徐孟、閭丘幸等持節 and lists 持節、都督、承制封拜 separately; offices 鎮軍將軍、平州刺史、大單于、遼東公 all kept, consistent with literal.

translationRepairs.before: Thereupon executed Ren’s placed guardians and magistrates, divided and moved great clans of Liaodong to Jicheng, established the three counties of Heyang, Wuci, and Xile, and returned.
translationRepairs.after: Thereupon he executed the guardians and magistrates Ren had installed, moved the great clans of Liaodong in groups to Jicheng, established the three counties of Heyang, Wuci, and Xile, and returned.
translationRepairs.reason: Adds the subject for 斬 and renders 仁所置守宰 and 分徙遼東大姓於棘城 accurately; the three counties 和陽、武次、西樂 retained.

translationRepairs.before: He executed Ren’s officials, relocated the leading Liaodong families to Jicheng, set up three new counties, and marched home.
translationRepairs.after: He executed Ren’s officials, relocated the leading Liaodong families to Jicheng, established the three counties of Heyang, Wuci, and Xile, and marched home.
translationRepairs.reason: Restores the omitted county names 和陽、武次、西樂 from 置和陽、武次、西樂三縣而歸, matching the literal field.

translationRepairs.before: He named Feng Yi chancellor, Han Shou marshal, and distributed ministerial and command posts among Pei Kai, Yang Wu, and the rest.
translationRepairs.after: He named Feng Yi state chancellor and Han Shou marshal, and appointed Pei Kai, Yang Wu, Wang Yu, Li Hong, Du Qun, Song Gai, Liu Zhan, Shi Cong, Huangfu Zhen, Yang Xie, Song Huang, Ping Xi, Zhang Hong and others as ministers and generals.
translationRepairs.reason: Restores all thirteen names in 裴開…張泓等並為列卿將帥 and 國相 as state chancellor, matching the literal list exactly.

translationRepairs.before: Jilong sent his general Ma Qiu leading host to welcome Liao; Ke ambushed seven thousand picked cavalry at Miyun Mountain, greatly defeated them, captured their marshal Yang Yu, general Xianyu Liang, and led Duan Liao and his division host back.
translationRepairs.after: Jilong sent his general Ma Qiu leading a host to meet Liao; Ke stationed seven thousand picked cavalry in ambush at Miyun Mountain and greatly defeated them, captured their marshal Yang Yu and general Xianyu Liang, and brought Duan Liao and his followers back.
translationRepairs.reason: 恪伏精騎七千於密雲山 means Ke placed his own cavalry in ambush; keeps 大敗之, 司馬陽裕, 將軍鮮于亮 and 及其部眾.

translationRepairs.before: Shi Hu sent Ma Qiu to fetch him; Murong Ke ambushed seven thousand elite riders at Miyun, captured Yang Yu and Xianyu Liang, and brought Duan Liao in.
translationRepairs.after: Shi Hu sent his general Ma Qiu with troops to meet Duan Liao. Murong Ke stationed seven thousand elite cavalry in ambush at Miyun Mountain and routed them, captured marshal Yang Yu and general Xianyu Liang, and brought Duan Liao and his followers back.
translationRepairs.reason: Restores 率眾, 大敗之, the roles 司馬/將軍, and 及其部眾, and correctly attributes the ambush 伏精騎七千 to Murong Ke.

translationRepairs.before: Although Huang styled King of Yan, there was yet no court command; thereupon sent his chief clerk Liu Xiang to present victory at the capital, concurrently stating the intent of provisional authority, and requesting a great campaign to pacify the Central Plain.
translationRepairs.after: Although Huang styled himself King of Yan, there was yet no court mandate; he thereupon sent his chief clerk Liu Xiang to report his victory at the capital, also explaining his provisional assumption of authority and requesting a great campaign to pacify the Central Plain.
translationRepairs.reason: Keeps 長史, 獻捷京師, 兼言權假之意 and 大舉討平中原; adds the needed reflexive for 稱燕王 without adding content.

translationRepairs.before: Though he called himself king of Yan, the court had not recognized it, so he sent Liu Xiang to report victories, explain his provisional rule, and ask for a northern expedition.
translationRepairs.after: Though he called himself King of Yan, he still lacked a court mandate, so he sent his chief clerk Liu Xiang to report his victory at the capital, explain his provisional assumption of authority, and ask for a major campaign to pacify the Central Plain.
translationRepairs.reason: Restores 長史, 京師 and 討平中原 (not merely a northern expedition); 未有朝命 as lacking a court mandate is accurate.

translationRepairs.before: Ke rode victory to pursue them, beheaded and captured over thirty thousand grades, built a fort at Fancheng and returned.
translationRepairs.after: Ke, riding the victory, pursued them, beheaded and captured over thirty thousand heads, built a garrison at Fancheng and returned.
translationRepairs.reason: 斬獲三萬餘級 kept as over thirty thousand, 乘勝 and 築戍凡城而還 rendered accurately as a garrison then return.

translationRepairs.before: Murong Ke pursued, killed or captured thirty thousand, and fortified Fancheng on the withdrawal.
translationRepairs.after: Murong Ke pressed the victory in pursuit, killed or captured over thirty thousand, built a garrison at Fancheng, and returned.
translationRepairs.reason: Restores 乘勝 and 餘 in 三萬餘級, and 築戍凡城而還 as building a garrison and returning rather than fortifying on withdrawal.

translationRepairs.before: Yu Bing, terrified yet unable to coerce him from afar, joined He Chong in recommending that the court recognize the title of king of Yan.
translationRepairs.after: On seeing the memorial and the letter, Yu Bing was greatly alarmed; because Huang was so far away and beyond his power to control, he joined He Chong and others in memorializing that Huang be allowed to style himself King of Yan.
translationRepairs.reason: Restores 見表及書 and 等 in 與何充等奏聽皝稱燕王; 以其絕遠，非所能制 rendered faithfully.

translationRepairs.before: Thereupon led cavalry twenty thousand out Wengong Pass, long drove reaching Ji city, advanced crossed Wusui Ford, entered Gaoyang; wherever passed burned granaries, plundered and moved You and Ji over thirty thousand households.
translationRepairs.after: Thereupon he led twenty thousand cavalry out through Yeweng Pass, drove straight to Ji city, advanced across Wusui Ford, and entered Gaoyang; wherever he passed he burned the stores, and he plundered and relocated more than thirty thousand households from You and Ji.
translationRepairs.reason: 蠮螉 read ye1 wēng per cited character databases, so Yeweng Pass; keeps 長驅, 武遂津, 焚燒積聚 and 三萬餘戶.

translationRepairs.before: He led twenty thousand horse through Wengong Pass, raced to Ji, crossed Wusui Ford into Gaoyang, burned depots, and carried off thirty thousand households from You and Ji.
translationRepairs.after: He then led twenty thousand cavalry out through Yeweng Pass, drove straight to Ji city, advanced across Wusui Ford into Gaoyang, burning the stores wherever he passed, and carried off more than thirty thousand households from You and Ji.
translationRepairs.reason: Uses Yeweng for 蠮螉塞 consistent with paired literal, restores 餘 in 三萬餘戶 and 薊城; worker 'Yiweng' in the reason is not adopted in the text.

translationRepairs.before: Murong Han shattered his army and took nearly every man alive.
translationRepairs.after: He sent Murong Han with cavalry to strike them; Moqian Hun was badly defeated and escaped alone, while his entire host was taken captive.
translationRepairs.reason: Restores 遣翰率騎擊之 and 僅以身免; 盡俘其眾 as entire host captured; Moqian Hun matches s0100 idiomatic.

translationRepairs.before: When Duan Liao asked Shi Hu for an escort, Yang Yu served as chief clerk under Ma Qiu.
translationRepairs.after: When Duan Liao asked Shi Hu to send troops to receive him, Yang Yu, while serving as Left Assistant, concurrently served as marshal to Ma Qiu, General Who Campaigns in the East.
translationRepairs.reason: 司馬 is marshal not chief clerk; restores 以左丞領 and the title 征東 for Ma Qiu, consistent with s0071 司馬 = marshal.

translationRepairs.before: At the time of Duan Liao’s request to welcome from Jilong, Yu as left assistant concurrently led Eastern Campaign Ma Qiu’s major.
translationRepairs.after: When Duan Liao requested that Jilong receive him, Yu, as Left Assistant, concurrently served as marshal to Ma Qiu, General Who Campaigns in the East.
translationRepairs.reason: 段遼之請迎于季龍 means Duan Liao asked Jilong to receive him; 以左丞領征東麻秋司馬 is a concurrent marshal post under the General Who Campaigns in the East.

translationRepairs.before: Even a county post can bless one’s heirs—let alone chancellor.
translationRepairs.after: Shaoyou said that a post as commandery clerk was enough to shelter one's descendants; how much more the post of chancellor of a state!
translationRepairs.reason: Restores the speaker 少遊 and renders 郡掾 as commandery clerk and 國相 as state chancellor; 廕後 as sheltering descendants is accurate.

translationRepairs.before: The Empress Dowager has died in indignation.
translationRepairs.after: And now the Empress Dowager, overcome with indignation, has suddenly passed away.
translationRepairs.reason: Proposed idiomatic restores 至今 as present-point transition, 發憤 as indignation, and 一旦 suddenness for 升遐; matches the Chinese against the incomplete before.

translationRepairs.before: The former king, by divine martial sage strategy, preserved one region; by might he destroyed traitors and by virtue he won the distant; therefore people of the nine provinces and foreign tribes beyond the frontier came carrying infants for ten thousand li, like infants returning to a loving father; the displaced exceeded the old population more than tenfold, the people were many and the land narrow, so those without fields were fourteen in ten.
translationRepairs.after: The former king, by divine martial sage strategy, preserved one region; by might he destroyed traitors and by virtue he won the distant; therefore people of the nine provinces and foreign tribes beyond the frontier came carrying infants for ten thousand li, like infants returning to a loving father; the displaced exceeded the old population more than tenfold, the people were many and the land narrow, so those without fields were four in ten.
translationRepairs.reason: 無田者十有四焉 in 人殷地狹 means four in ten, not fourteen in ten; the proposed literal correctly repairs the quantity while preserving all other propositions.

translationRepairs.before: Murong Hui, by divine martial strategy, preserved this region, destroyed traitors by might and won the distant by virtue; people of the nine provinces and foreign tribes came carrying infants for ten thousand li like children to a loving father. Refugees outnumbered the old population more than tenfold; land was scarce and fourteen in ten had no fields.
translationRepairs.after: Murong Hui, by divine martial strategy, preserved this region, destroyed traitors by might and won the distant by virtue; people of the nine provinces and foreign tribes came carrying infants for ten thousand li like children to a loving father. Refugees outnumbered the old population more than tenfold; land was scarce and four in ten had no fields.
translationRepairs.reason: Same 十有四 quantity fix as the literal pair; idiomatic now reads four in ten and keeps 先王 deeds, 繈負萬里, and refugee scale intact.

translationRepairs.before: Moreover flood and drought are misfortunes Yao and Tang did not escape; a king ought to dredge and maintain canals and ditches, follow the irrigation methods of Zheng Bai, Ximen, and Shi Qi; in drought open ditches as rain, in flood send water into channels; above no worry like the "Cloudy Han," below no trouble of mire and flood.
translationRepairs.after: Moreover flood and drought are misfortunes Yao and Tang did not escape; a king ought to dredge and maintain canals and ditches, following the Zheng and Bai canals and the irrigation methods of Ximen and Shi Qi; in drought open ditches as rain, in flood send water into channels; above no worry like the "Yunhan," below no trouble of mire and flood.
translationRepairs.reason: 鄭白 are the Zheng and Bai canals, not a person parallel to 西門 and 史起; restoring canal names and 《雲漢》 as Yunhan matches the Chinese.

translationRepairs.before: Flood and drought, which Yao and Tang did not escape, require dredged canals and irrigation like Zheng Bai, Ximen, and Shi Qi; drought is eased by channels and flood by drainage, ending worry above and mire below.
translationRepairs.after: Flood and drought, which Yao and Tang did not escape, require dredged canals and irrigation after the Zheng and Bai canals and the methods of Ximen and Shi Qi; drought is eased by opening channels to supply water like rain, and floodwaters are directed into drainage channels, so that above there is no anxiety like that expressed in Yunhan and below there is no misery from inundation.
translationRepairs.reason: Idiomatic likewise separates Zheng and Bai canals from Ximen and Shi Qi, and restores 決溝為雨, 入於溝瀆, and Yunhan anxiety versus 昏墊.

translationRepairs.before: Huang issued an edict: “Feng Yu’s words frighten me.
translationRepairs.after: Huang then issued an order, saying: “On reading the remonstrance of Recorder Feng, I am truly afraid.
translationRepairs.reason: Restores 乃令曰, 覽, and title 封記室 omitted in the before; Recorder Feng for 封記室 fits the remonstrance scene.

translationRepairs.before: The heartland is still at war, so I cannot yet cut official posts.
translationRepairs.after: The heartland is not yet pacified, warfare does not cease, and many have rendered meritorious and loyal service, so the official establishment cannot be reduced.
translationRepairs.reason: Covers 中州未平, 兵難不息, 勳誠既多, and 官僚不可以減也 without softening the ban on cutting posts.

translationRepairs.before: Ministers who speak truth deserve patience—ignore wild rumors but heed good counsel.
translationRepairs.after: For a minister to offer words that touch his ruler is most difficult; wild and baseless matters should all be brushed aside without inquiry, while one chooses what is good and follows it.
translationRepairs.reason: Restores 關言於人主至難也 and the full 妖妄不經…擇其善者而從之 counsel structure against the compressed before.

translationRepairs.before: Restore censured advisers to their posts.
translationRepairs.after: They may all be restored to their original offices and still serve in the remonstrance bureau.
translationRepairs.reason: Restores 悉, 本官, and 仍居諫司 that the before collapsed into a bare restore.

translationRepairs.before: Award him fifty thousand cash and invite anyone, high or low, to criticize me freely.”
translationRepairs.after: So award him fifty thousand cash, and clearly announce inside and outside that whoever wishes to state my faults, whether noble or base, need have no taboo.”
translationRepairs.reason: Restores 明宣內外 and 有欲陳孤過者，不拘貴賤，勿有所諱 beside the fifty thousand cash award.

translationRepairs.before: Elated, he returned, proclaimed an amnesty, renamed the palace Helong, and built a Buddhist monastery on the height.
translationRepairs.after: Huang was greatly pleased, returned to the palace, pardoned those within his borders, named the new palace Helong, and built the Longxiang Buddhist monastery on the mountain.
translationRepairs.reason: Restores 皝大悅, 赦其境內, 號新宮曰和龍, and the named 龍翔佛寺 omitted as a generic monastery.

translationRepairs.before: Huang greatly pleased, returned palace, pardoned those within his borders, styled the new palace Helong, established Dragon-Soar Buddha temple on the mountain.
translationRepairs.after: Huang was greatly pleased, returned to the palace, pardoned those within his borders, named the new palace Helong, and established the Longxiang Buddhist temple on the mountain.
translationRepairs.reason: Aligns the temple name as Longxiang with 龍翔 and keeps 赦其境內 and 號新宮曰和龍 in the literal field.

translationRepairs.before: He wrote a primer to replace the Rush to Literacy and fifteen moral essays for the royal sons.
translationRepairs.after: He personally composed the Taishang Chapter to replace the Jijiu, and also wrote fifteen chapters of Canonical Admonitions to teach the sons of the nobility.
translationRepairs.reason: Restores proper titles 《太上章》,《急就》, and 《典誡》十五篇 for teaching 胄子.

translationRepairs.before: Personally composed the “Supreme Lord Chapter” to replace the “Rush to Literacy,” also wrote fifteen pieces of “Classic Admonitions,” to teach the sons of the house.
translationRepairs.after: He personally composed the Taishang Chapter to replace the Jijiu, and also wrote fifteen chapters of Canonical Admonitions, to teach the sons of the nobility.
translationRepairs.reason: Literal now matches those three titles and renders 胄子 as sons of the nobility rather than narrowing to the house alone.

translationRepairs.before: Murong Ke seized Nansu from Goguryeo and left a garrison.
translationRepairs.after: Murong Ke attacked Goguryeo’s Nansu, took it, posted a garrison, and returned.
translationRepairs.reason: Restores 攻, 克之, 置戍, and 而還 against the before that dropped the attack verb and return.

translationRepairs.before: In his third regnal year he sent Murong Jun and Murong Ke with seventeen thousand horse against Puyu; they captured the king and fifty thousand subjects.
translationRepairs.after: In the third year he sent his heir Jun and Ke with seventeen thousand cavalry to raid Puyu eastward; they took it, captured its king and more than fifty thousand of the tribe, and returned.
translationRepairs.reason: Bare 三年 is third year not regnal year; restores 世子俊, 東襲, 五萬餘, and 以還 with the cavalry count.

translationRepairs.before: Yet the Hu still hold the Central Plain; I had hoped to cleanse them for Murong Hui’s sake.
translationRepairs.after: But the rebel Hu barbarians straddle and hold the Divine Land, and the Central Plain is not yet pacified. I always steeled my heart and swore that I would swallow up the vile caitiffs, above to fulfil the late king's dying wish and below to discharge my duty to the realm between the mountains and the sea.
translationRepairs.reason: Restores 常克心自誓, 志吞醜虜, 上成先王遺旨, and 下謝山海之責 omitted in the short before.

translationRepairs.before: But the rebellious Hu stride occupying the divine continent; the central plain is not yet quieted; Han constantly set heart to swear, intent to swallow the ugly bandits, above to complete the late king’s leftover command, below to apologize for the duty to mountains and seas.
translationRepairs.after: But the rebellious Hu occupy the Divine Land, and the Central Plain is not yet pacified; Han has always steeled his heart and sworn an oath, intent on swallowing up the vile enemies, above to fulfil the late king's last instructions and below to discharge his duty to the land of mountains and seas.
translationRepairs.reason: Fixes misleading apologize for 下謝山海之責 to discharge the duty, while keeping the oath, 醜虜 aim, and 先王遺旨.

translationRepairs.before: As for minister’s presenting words to the lord sovereign—most difficult; demonic and wild not-classic matters all ought to be swept away unasked; choose the good of them and follow them.
translationRepairs.after: For a minister to present words to his sovereign is most difficult; absurd and unfounded matters should all be set aside without inquiry, while one chooses what is good and follows it.
translationRepairs.reason: 夫人臣關言於人主，至難也 is rendered fully; 妖妄不經之事皆應蕩然不問 as absurd unfounded matters set aside without inquiry; 擇其善者而從之 with neutral 'one' correctly keeps the sovereign as the chooser.

translationRepairs.before: As the Odes says, “No good word goes unanswered.”
translationRepairs.after: As the Odes says, “No word goes unanswered.”
translationRepairs.reason: 無言不酬 contains no 善, so 'good word' is an addition; 'No word goes unanswered' matches the source and the paired literal 'No word without answer'.

translationRepairs.before: The beasts intertwined, sported in the air, dropped their horns, and flew away.
translationRepairs.after: The two dragons crossed their heads, sported and soared, shed their horns, and departed.
translationRepairs.reason: 二龍交首嬉翔，解角而去 names two dragons and 交首; the replacement restores both, keeps 嬉翔 and 解角而去, and matches the paired literal.

translationRepairs.before: Duan Juan, Xianbei chieftain and Jin general, sought him eagerly.
translationRepairs.after: At that time the Xianbei shanyu Duan Juan, who held the Jin titles of General of Agile Cavalry and Duke of Liaoxi, had a refined fondness for men of talent and humbly invited Yang Yu.
translationRepairs.reason: Proposed idiomatic restores 時, romanizes 單于 as shanyu, and recovers 晉驃騎大將軍, 遼西公, 雅好人物, and 虛心延裕 against the compressed before.
